name: NTFS Alternate Data Streams (ADS) - Hidden File Content
description: NTFS Alternate Data Streams (ADS) allow storing additional data streams alongside a file's default $DATA stream. Attackers and CTF authors hide flags, credentials, or payloads in ADS. A normal 'dir' or 'type' won't show them - you need 'dir /r' to list streams and 'more <' or PowerShell to read them.
notes:
=== DISCOVERY ===
  dir /r                          # List ALL streams (ADS show as filename:streamname:$DATA)
  dir /r C:\Users\*\Desktop\      # Check user desktops

=== READING ADS ===
  more < hm.txt:root.txt          # Read the 'root.txt' stream hidden inside hm.txt
  more < hm.txt:root.txt:$DATA    # Explicit $DATA stream reference
  # 'type' does NOT work with ADS - use 'more <'

=== POWERSHELL ===
  Get-Item -Path hm.txt -Stream *                     # List all streams
  Get-Content -Path hm.txt -Stream root.txt           # Read a specific stream
  Get-ChildItem -Recurse | ForEach-Object { Get-Item $_.FullName -Stream * } 2>$null  # Recursive scan

=== CREATING ADS (for testing/understanding) ===
  echo 'hidden content' > normal.txt:secret.txt       # Write to ADS
  notepad normal.txt:secret.txt                       # Open ADS in notepad

=== EXTRACTING FILES FROM ADS ===
  # ADS can hide executables, not just text:
  expand filename.txt:hidden.exe hidden.exe            # Extract hidden exe
  # Or with PowerShell:
  Get-Content filename.txt -Stream hidden.exe -Encoding Byte | Set-Content hidden.exe -Encoding Byte

=== WHERE TO LOOK ===
- User desktops (flag hiding in CTFs)
- Temp directories
- Application data
- Downloaded files (Zone.Identifier stream marks downloads)

examples.label: Read hidden stream from a file
PowerShell - list all streams on a file

references.title: MITRE T1564.004 - Hide Artifacts: NTFS File Attributes

defense.why_it_works: NTFS supports multiple named data streams per file. The default stream ($DATA) is what normal tools show. Additional streams are invisible to dir, type, and most file managers, making them effective for hiding data.
defense.prerequisites: NTFS filesystem; access to the file containing the ADS.
defense.impact: Discovery of hidden credentials, flags, or payloads that standard enumeration misses.
defense.detection: [MITRE T1564.004] Sysmon Event 15 (FileCreateStreamHash) logs ADS creation; dir /r or streams.exe in command history.
defense.artifacts: Sysmon Event 15 for stream creation; PowerShell script block logs showing Get-Item -Stream; command history with 'dir /r'.
defense.splunk_spl:
index=sysmon EventCode=15
| where NOT match(TargetFilename, "Zone\.Identifier")
| table _time, Image, TargetFilename, Hash
defense.sentinel_kql:
SysmonEvent
| where EventID == 15
| where TargetFilename !contains "Zone.Identifier"
| project TimeGenerated, Image, TargetFilename, Hashes
defense.prevention: Monitor Sysmon Event 15 for ADS creation (exclude Zone.Identifier); use streams.exe (Sysinternals) for periodic ADS audits; restrict write access to sensitive directories.

detections.name: NTFS Alternate Data Stream creation (non-ZoneIdentifier)
detections.logic:
SysmonEvent
| where EventID == 15
| where TargetFilename !contains "Zone.Identifier"
| project TimeGenerated, Image, TargetFilename, Hashes
| sort by TimeGenerated desc
detections.false_positives: Some applications legitimately use ADS for metadata storage
detections.tuning: Exclude known legitimate ADS users; focus on ADS in user-writable directories
